- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to avoid mean reversion miss.
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply slight downward bias (−0.5% to −2%) to first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive sentiment followed by a drop, model often fails to adjust downward; apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 days after sentiment drop.
- Model tends to ignore recent price volatility in favor of historical mean; if recent 18-day range is wide, apply volatility-weighted adjustment to forecast.
